newsitem.title: USA: Judge rules Orange County lawsuit can proceed.
newsitem.headline: Judge rules Orange County lawsuit can proceed.

text.p: A federal judge has ruled that Orange County, California, can proceed with its bankruptcy-related lawsuit against the U.S. Office of Finance, attorneys said on Thursday.
County attorney Michael Swartz said the ruling, by U.S. District Judge Gary Taylor, cleared the way for the case to proceed toward trial.

Earlier this week, U.S. Department of Justice lawyers urged Taylor to dismiss the lawsuit, which names the United States and the Office of Finance as defendants along with the Federal Home Loan Banks.
Taylor denied the request, ruling that the court "cannot find immunity as a matter of law."
The Federal Home Loan Bank System supplies credit reserves for savings and loans, cooperative banks and other mortgage lenders. It is made up of 12 Federal Home Loan Banks.

The county sued the banks in December 1996, alleging that false and misleading misrepresentations and omissions were contained in their offering circulars. The county further alleged that the Office of Finance acted as the "fiscal agent" for the banks in transactions involving risky securities.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection in December 1994 after sustaining losses estimated at more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy one year ago.
